transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm just... having some trouble keeping things together at work. I'm a software developer, but I also do some other things, and... I just can't seem to organize all the moving parts anymore. There are patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions... and I just end up starting whatever is loudest instead of what actually matters. It's getting to be a problem.
Do you find it hard to stay organized or focused on tasks outside of work, like at home or in social situations?

I don't know... I haven't really thought about it. Work is where all the pressure is. 

At home, it's just... I don't really notice it being as much of a problem. I guess there's just less to keep track of.
Do you ever find yourself struggling with focus or organization in situations outside of work, like during conversations, while running errands, or when doing chores at home?

I mean... not really. Chores are just chores, I guess. They get done eventually. I don't really think about it. 

And errands are fine. It's... it's mostly just the work stuff that I'm worried about.
Have you ever found it difficult to stay focused or organized during conversations, while running errands, or when doing tasks at home?

I... I thought we just went over that. Like I said, no, not really. 

I don't really analyze how I do chores or run errands. They just get done. And conversations are... fine. I don't know what else to tell you about that. I'm really just here because my job is becoming a mess.
Have you ever noticed yourself forgetting things, getting distracted, or having trouble organizing your thoughts during everyday activities, even if just slightly?

I don't... I mean, I guess everyone forgets things sometimes. But it's not something I really keep track of. Like I keep saying, I'm just struggling at work. That's the only thing that's really bothering me.

Can you recall any recent situations outside of work—like during conversations, while doing something at home, or running errands—where you found yourself unusually forgetful, easily distracted, or struggling to keep your thoughts organized?

Look... I don't know why you keep asking me the exact same thing. No. I can't think of anything. 

It's just my job. I really don't have anything else to tell you about the rest of it.

Looking back over the past few months, have you noticed any situations outside of work—like at home, in social settings, or during personal tasks—where you had clear difficulty staying focused, organizing tasks, or remembering important details?

I... I feel like we're going in circles here. I really don't know how else to answer this. 

No. I haven't noticed anything like that. It's just work. I don't know why we keep focusing on everything else when work is the only place I'm having trouble.

Looking back, can you think of even one situation outside of work—like at home, with friends, or during a personal project—where you clearly noticed yourself being more forgetful, distracted, or disorganized?

I... I don't know what else to say. I really can't think of anything. 

Like I said, it's just work. I'm just trying to figure out why I'm struggling so much there. I don't... I don't have anything else to add.
Have you ever had trouble staying focused or keeping things organized when you're not at work—like when you're reading something for fun, listening to music, or just relaxing at home?
I just... no. I read fine. If I'm relaxing, I'm just relaxing. I don't know why we're still on this. It's really just the job.
Looking back, have you ever noticed even small moments—like misplacing everyday items, losing your train of thought mid-conversation, or forgetting part of a plan—when you weren’t at work?
No. I mean... no. I don't lose my train of thought or forget plans. I just... I don't know how many different ways I can say it. It's really just the job.
Looking back, were you ever noticeably forgetful, distracted, or had trouble staying organized as a child or teenager, even if it wasn't a big problem back then?

I... I suppose. When I was younger. Grade school, mostly. 

Teachers used to write notes... saying I was bright, but that I daydreamed. I guess I used to lose my homework folders back then. Or I'd finish an assignment and just... forget to actually turn it in. But that was... I mean, that was a long time ago, before I was even a teenager.
Looking back, were you noticeably distracted, forgetful, or had trouble staying organized before age 12—even if it wasn’t a major issue at the time?
I think... I just answered that. Yeah. The daydreaming and the folders, that was all in grade school. So, before twelve, yes.
Looking back, were you noticeably distracted, forgetful, or had trouble staying organized before age 12—even if it wasn’t a major issue at the time?
I... I just said yes. That was all in grade school. So, yes, before I was twelve.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did those early difficulties with daydreaming and losing homework happen mostly in one place, like just at school, or did they also affect other parts of your life back then?
I don't really remember... mostly school, I guess. I mean, my parents probably got annoyed if I forgot to do my chores or lost my jacket, but... it was mostly school stuff that got noticed.
Looking back at when you were in grade school, did the difficulties you had with daydreaming and losing homework happen only at school, or did they also affect other parts of your life back then?
I... didn't you just ask me that? Like I said, it was mostly school. And at home, with chores and things. I don't really have anything else to add to that. I just don't remember much else.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did the difficulties you had with daydreaming and losing homework also affect other areas of your life, like home or social situations, or was it mostly just a problem at school?
I... we just went over this. It was school, and home. I don't know what else you want me to say. I really don't remember anything else from back then.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did your difficulties with daydreaming and losing homework cause any clear problems at home or in other settings, like trouble completing tasks or following through on directions, or was it mainly just an issue at school?
I... look, we've covered this three times now. It was school. And home, like I said before. I don't... I just don't have anything else to tell you about it.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did your difficulties with daydreaming and losing homework clearly interfere with your ability to complete tasks or follow through at home, or was it mainly just an issue at school without affecting your functioning at home?

I... I really don't know why we keep going in circles with this. I told you, it was school... and home. I don't remember the exact details of how it interfered, just that I'd get yelled at for not doing my chores. I don't know what else to say.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did your difficulties with daydreaming and losing homework clearly interfere with your ability to complete tasks or follow through at home or in other settings, such as with friends or during extracurricular activities?
I... look, we've been over this. I just don't remember it affecting my friends or... or clubs, or whatever. I don't know. It was just school and home. That's all I've got.

Looking back at when you were in grade school, did your difficulties with daydreaming and losing homework clearly interfere with your ability to complete tasks or follow through at home or with friends, or was it mainly just an issue at school?
I... I really don't know what else you want me to say about this. I just answered it. It was school and home. I don't have any other details to give you. Can we please just move on?

These symptoms align with the diagnostic criteria for ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation, particularly the requirement for symptoms to be present in more than one setting during childhood and to persist into adulthood with functional impairment in multiple domains.
